Use Tier 2: add a jointly trained long-term preference module to ConvRec while retaining its existing sequence backbone, including the attention block from the latest attempt. Focus on model_design and training_evaluation. The attention-augmented model reached 0.5038 macro HR@10, with Electronics at 0.380 versus the SASRec baseline’s 0.420; this motivates testing whether a persistent preference representation helps when recent transitions provide weak evidence.

At each sequence position, compute the padding-masked cumulative mean of the shared input item embeddings using only the observed prefix. Transform this mean through a learned linear projection and LayerNorm, then compute a per-dimension sigmoid gate from the concatenation of this preference vector and the existing backbone state. Fuse the two representations through that gate and apply the existing final normalization before scoring with the shared item embeddings and jointly learned item bias. This adds an explicit path for persistent user interests without requiring additional attention layers or independently fitted predictors, and its cumulative computation adds little sequence-length overhead.

Keep the sampler, 32-negative cross-entropy, optimizer, schedule, batch size, seeds, epoch limit, and checkpoint selection rule unchanged so this experiment isolates the representation change. Update the predictor writer to instantiate the revised architecture and strictly load exactly one selected checkpoint per category, preserving all four routes and identical history packing during validation and inference. Check causal prefix behavior, finite padding handling, and checkpoint reload parity, then assess the change using the pinned host’s actual macro HR@10 and category results. Preserve supplied splits, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, and single-GPU execution; leave held-out prediction generation to the host without reading test files.
